title: Mapping the Homogeneity Landscape Across Safety-Critical Task Types

original_idea.title: Mapping the Homogeneity Landscape Across Safety-Critical Task Types
original_idea.problem: We do not know whether the Artificial Hivemind effect is stronger, weaker, or differently shaped on safety-relevant tasks compared to open-ended creative tasks.
original_idea.direction: Extend the Infinity-Chat methodology to a curated set of safety-critical prompt categories and measure intra- and inter-model similarity scores across 10+ models using existing embeddings tools.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If safety outputs are even more homogeneous than creative outputs, a single shared blind spot becomes a systemic vulnerability rather than an isolated failure.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind (NeurIPS 2025) found pronounced inter-model homogeneity on 26K open-ended queries; AILuminate benchmark tests 12 safety hazard categories with 24K+ prompts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if safety outputs are more homogeneous than creative outputs, this directly reveals a systemic vulnerability that the safety community needs to address.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: requires embedding computation and pairwise similarity analysis across 10+ models, which is feasible but not trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: running 10+ models across multiple safety categories and computing similarity matrices is substantial for a 30-hour project.

novelty.reasoning: The Artificial Hivemind paper (NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper) established inter-model homogeneity on 26K open-ended queries using Infinity-Chat. However, it focused on open-ended creative/general queries, not safety-critical task types specifically. No published work extends the Artificial Hivemind methodology to safety-specific prompt categories (e.g., AILuminate hazard categories). The proposal to compare homogeneity levels between safety tasks and creative tasks is a natural but unexplored extension.
